title: What is the current meta for developing games with AI?
author: Bitter-College8786
selftext:
This infographic is just there to pull people into reading what I am asking.

Is there some kind of a meta when you develop games with AI agents?  
Like which engine to use? Which 3D generation tools etc.?

comments.author: Disastrous-Round-150
comments.body: I love doing it 100% from scratch zero engines, zero assets 100% procedural!

replies.author: rooktko
replies.body: Got any procedural assets you can show us? What’s your system for it?

comments.author: Clayrone
comments.body: I think Blockbench could also be in the 3D section. Great tool, without steep learning curve.

comments.author: Binary-Trees
comments.body: Im using pixelorama instead of aspsrite, it works great and has a CLI. And its free.

comments.author: Niroooooo
comments.body: I think hunyuan3d 2.1 is missing, it's a great free option if your machine can run it locally.

replies.author: tuptain
replies.body: Hunyuan carries a restrictive license, use Tripo, $20 a month gets tons of assets generated.

comments.author: Asmardos1
comments.body: Depends on the game you want to make therefore there is no universal meta

comments.author: lamachejo
comments.body: Is spine usable with AI now?? Is there an mco or whats the workflow?

replies.author: gamedevjp
replies.body: I’d like to know this as well. I don’t believe there is a Spine MCP

comments.author: sunnystormy64
comments.body: This is misleading and heavily opinionated. I have plenty of local models and fine-tunes that buck this infographic. I think you need to explore local models more before making a premature "meta" claim.

replies.author: Tyalou
replies.body: This is fairly accurate but yes, there are shortcuts and custom build that will get there faster/cheaper than spending... And sometimes, spending is the only way to get clean output.

comments.author: HugoDzz
comments.body:
\- No engine  
\- Raw TS (or C for native / retro console)  
\- Procedural for VFX  
\- Sprite Fusion for pixel art

comments.author: SchmidlMeThis
comments.body: To answer the question, I think it really depends on what kind of game you want to make. This infographics shows a lot of possible routes but, just like game design pre-AI, it can vary a lot based on the end goal.

comments.author: bigsmokaaaa
comments.body: I'd suggest Kimodo for 3D animation, it's like open source cascadeur from nvidia. This is a terrific list btw

comments.author: eldudebrothr
comments.body: and i thought being an ai game dev meant you dont need 666 different subs lol

comments.author: No-Trouble-9138
comments.body: No video tools? I generate then on Plyry.

comments.author: PeanutSilent884
comments.body: Asset libraries : fab, polyhaven ambientcg. World generators : gaea ,world creator etc

comments.author: AuraTickler
comments.body:
Where is my boy libgdx with java/kotlin?

Currently making a 2D game with it
